neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were relatives with a prior incident between them. On the night of the incident, the victim and his wife woke up, and while the wife prepared for cooking, the victim went to attend to nature's call. The wife heard the victim shouting and ran to the scene, where she saw two of the accused assaulting the victim with an axe while the other two held him. The victim was taken to the hospital and declared dead. The accused were charged with murder under Section 302 of the IPC read with Section 34. The trial court acquitted two accused, finding they did not participate in the assault. The High Court reversed the acquittal, finding a common intention among all accused to cause death.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that there was a common intention among all the accused to cause the death of the victim, supported by the presence of all four accused at the scene with weapons and the testimony of the wife of the deceased.

the presence of all four accused on the spot in the night/early morning, armed with dangerous weapons

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the appellants only held the deceased without participating in the actual assault or using a weapon, and thus should not be held liable for the murder.

quotes.text: the role attributed to the appellants was of catching the victim without actual participation or use of weapon to assault and inflict the injuries
as that was the only role, it could not be said that there was a shared common intention along with the first two accused to cause death

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle of constructive liability under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, emphasizing the need for a common intention and participation in the criminal act.

quotes.text: s.34 creates a deeming fiction by infusing and importing a criminal act constituting an offence committed by one, into others, in pursuance to a common intention
the dominant feature of s.34 is an element of intention and participation in action
